descriptionChirho: A masculine noun meaning 'oak' or 'terebinth,' referring to large deciduous trees often associated with sacred sites and place-names in the Hebrew Bible (e.g., 'oak of Moreh,' 'oaks of Mamre'). All 9 occurrences share a single botanical referent with variation only in number and grammatical state: singular construct 'oak of' (eng: oak-of, arb: بَلُّوطَة, kor: 상수리나무, swa: mwaloni), plural construct with preposition 'in/by oaks of' (arb: عِنْدَ–بَلُّوطَاتِ / فِي–بَلُوطَاتِ, spa: en–encinas–de, swa: katika–mialoni–ya), and plain plural construct 'oaks of' (arb: بَلُوطَاتِ, hin: बलूतों–के). Spanish uses both 'encina' and 'roble' for this single referent.
